classification.class: unsafe shell expansion of untrusted path
classification.classification_note: ARVO metadata leaves this sample unclassified. The saved Stage 01 symptom is an AddressSanitizer `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` inside libc `wordexp`, but the patched project-side defect is tinygltf performing shell-style pathname expansion on attacker-controlled glTF image URIs.

bug_description.original: The vulnerability allows unnecessary expansion of file paths for glTF asset paths (URIs), which introduces a security risk due to the use of `wordexp`.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 589-byte witness is a JSON glTF document with one `images[0].uri` string. `tinygltf::ParseImage()` materializes that attacker-controlled URI, but vulnerable `IsDataURI()` recognizes only a small fixed set of exact `data:*;base64,` prefixes, and the witness begins with the malformed literal `data:888...`, so parsing falls into the external-file branch. `dlib::urldecode()` then derives `decoded_uri` from the URI text, `FindFile()` forwards the first search candidate into `ExpandFilePath()` before any existence check, and vulnerable `ExpandFilePath()` wraps the path in quotes and calls `wordexp(..., 0)` on it. The saved AddressSanitizer run immediately crashes with a wild-address READ / SEGV inside libc `wordexp`. The fixing patch removes this expansion entirely and returns `filepath` unchanged.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the vulnerability-relevant attacker data. `ParseImage()` reads the image object's `uri` member into local string `uri`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 589-byte JSON document with one `images[0].uri` string. This statement materializes that exact string; it starts with `data:888888...` instead of any supported `data:*;base64,` header and later contains shell-expansion syntax `${...}` in the same URI text.
source.note: This is the first project statement on the crashing path that turns the attacker-controlled JSON field into the `uri` value later passed to path handling.

sink.description: Project-side sink. `ExpandFilePath()` passes the attacker-controlled URI-derived path into libc `wordexp`, which is the immediate callee on the saved AddressSanitizer crash stack.
sink.note: The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` shows frame 3 at `tiny_gltf.h:2646` in `tinygltf::ExpandFilePath`, followed immediately by libc `wordexp`, where the READ / SEGV is reported.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Vulnerable `ExpandFilePath()` performs shell-style expansion with `wordexp` on an attacker-controlled glTF URI-derived path instead of treating that value as a literal file path.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch replaces this whole expansion path with `return filepath;` and comments that glTF URIs should not use `wordexp` for security reasons.

parser_admitted.description: After the top-level JSON is accepted and the `images` array is iterated, `LoadFromString()` enters `ParseImage()` on the attacker-controlled image object, reaching the `uri` parsing path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted value begins as the parsed `uri` string from the JSON image object. Later steps reject it as a supported data URI, URL-decode it, and feed the resulting path text into `wordexp`.

coarse_trace.summary: The saved JSON witness is admitted as a glTF document, the `images` array is iterated, and control enters `ParseImage()` for the attacker-controlled image object.
`ParseImage()` materializes `images[0].uri`, rejects it as a supported embedded data URI, URL-decodes it, and routes it into external-file loading.
External-file lookup expands the URI-derived path with `FsCallbacks::ExpandFilePath` before checking whether any candidate file exists.
`ExpandFilePath()` quotes the path and calls libc `wordexp`, reaching the observed AddressSanitizer SEGV inside `wordexp`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `ParseImage()` reads the attacker-controlled `uri` member out of the image JSON object and materializes it in local string `uri`.

The witness URI does not start with any exact header accepted by `IsDataURI()` (`data:application/octet-stream;base64,`, `data:image/*;base64,`, `data:text/plain;base64,`, or `data:application/gltf-buffer;base64,`). Because it begins with malformed `data:888...`, this guard is false and parsing takes the external-file branch.

`ParseImage()` URL-decodes the attacker string before filesystem lookup. The saved witness contains many `+` characters and a `%` sequence, so `decoded_uri` is a transformed path string, not a byte-for-byte copy of the raw JSON `uri`.

The external-image path forwards `decoded_uri` into `LoadExternalFile()` as the filename to search. On the saved fuzzer call, `base_dir` / `basedir` is the empty string, so lookup starts from `""` and then `"."`.

Before any `FileExists` check, `FindFile()` expands each search candidate. `LoadExternalFile()` has just built `paths = { basedir, "." }`; with the saved `basedir == ""`, the first `JoinPath(paths[i], filepath)` returns the attacker-derived `filepath` unchanged, so `ExpandFilePath()` receives the decoded URI string directly.
`ExpandFilePath()` does not treat the path as a literal filename. It builds `quoted_path` by surrounding the attacker-derived path with double quotes as the input string for shell-style expansion.

Root cause and sink. Vulnerable `ExpandFilePath()` invokes libc `wordexp` with flags 0 on the attacker-derived path string. The saved AddressSanitizer stack immediately enters libc `wordexp` from this statement and crashes on a READ / SEGV there. The fix removes this call and returns `filepath` unchanged.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. Fine-trace step 7 is the project-side `wordexp` call at `tiny_gltf.h:2646`, and the saved ASan crash is the immediately nested libc `wordexp` frame reached from that statement.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `ExpandFilePath -> FindFile -> LoadExternalFile -> ParseImage -> LoadFromString -> LoadASCIIFromString -> fuzz_gltf`, which matches the rebuilt source path exactly.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The parsed `uri` from step 1 survives the `!IsDataURI(uri)` branch, is transformed into `decoded_uri` by `urldecode`, is forwarded into `FindFile`, and then becomes `quoted_path` for the `wordexp` sink.

poc.trigger: Feed the staged JSON witness to the saved `fuzz_gltf` harness. tinygltf parses `images[0].uri`, falls into the external-image path, and crashes inside libc `wordexp` from `tinygltf::ExpandFilePath`.

format.name: JSON glTF document
format.contract: The exact staged 589-byte JSON witness saved as `poc`: a glTF document with one `images[0].uri` string whose prefix is malformed `data:888...` rather than any header recognized by `IsDataURI()`, so tinygltf takes the external-image branch and later calls `wordexp` on the URL-decoded path text. The saved evidence establishes only this exact witness, not a broader class of URIs or shell-expansion patterns.
